[LEXP.3.6.1] **`degrees` and `radians` are this composition, and no other.** With
$\hat\pi$ the `Float` `math.pi` ([LIMP.3.3.4]) and $\circ(\cdot)$ the binary64
nearest a real value, ties to even:

$$\operatorname{degrees}(x) = \circ\!\left(x \times \circ\!\left(\frac{180}{\hat\pi}\right)\right), \qquad \operatorname{radians}(x) = \circ\!\left(x \times \circ\!\left(\frac{\hat\pi}{180}\right)\right)$$

Each factor is the exact quotient rounded once, a constant of the language; the
engine must evaluate each function as one correctly rounded multiplication by it
([LDET.3.6.1]), and the compiler must fold a constant operand the same way
([LEXP.8.8]). An `Int` argument is converted to `Float` first ([LEXP.7.3]). At a
non-finite or NaN argument the result is the IEEE 754 product's ([LDET.3.6.2]).
